Description: Main microcontroller board with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, used to host the web server, fetch NTP time, and control the RF transmitter.
Notes: Hosts the web server, connects to pool.ntp.org, and executes the control logic. No external RTC module needed.

Description: Low-cost 433.92MHz RF transmitter module to send wireless control signals to the outdoor lights.
Notes: Connects GND to Arduino GND, VCC to 5V, and DATA to Pin 10. Uses the RCSwitch library.

Component: 433MHz RF Controlled Outdoor Light / Outlet Receiver
Description: Outdoor-rated wireless smart plug or light fixture that responds to the 433MHz RF signal code (e.g., code 11206632).
Notes: Needs to be paired with or capable of learning/responding to the transmitted 24-bit RF signal.

Description: Cable to program the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi and provide 5V power.
Notes: Arduino UNO R4 uses USB-C (unlike older UNO boards which used USB-B).

Description: Premium jumper wires for making secure connections between the Arduino and the RF Transmitter.
Notes: Required connections: GND to GND, VCC to 5V, and DATA to Pin 10.

Description: Half-size breadboard for prototyping connections easily without soldering.
Notes: Optional but recommended for organizing wiring during testing.

Description: Standard USB wall adapter to power the Arduino continuously once programmed.
Notes: Powers the setup continuously once deployed near your network / window.
